rationale: The opening reply was correct and well-pitched: 'completely normal for the sides of a modern fridge-freezer to become warm' with the condenser built into the side panels and no fire risk. It then drifted into treating the tight alcove as a fault, with headings like 'Inadequate ventilation due to tight alcove causing overheating of condenser coils', and the second and third replies are near-identical repeats of '1cm is not enough... check the manual'. It never asked the key hazard-ruling checks (plug warmth, fridge/freezer temperatures, is it cooling well) and gave no concrete figures despite being given the exact model, so the customer ends mildly more worried than needed, though nothing unsafe or fabricated was said and pointing to the manual and Hotpoint is reasonable.
